doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Mario Bauza recommends him to Dizzy Gillespie for a Fat Tuesday gig
summary: Six months after arriving, Mario Bauza calls him to fill in for Dizzy's drummer, stuck in a snowstorm, at Fat Tuesday.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And here you are, you’re in the country for about a year and can you tell me how all of a sudden you appear in a club as Dizzy Gillespie’s drummer?

Life is full of surprises. I arrived to New York and I got in touch with the Cuban musician Mario Bauza who was responsible for that Afro-Cuban jazz movement in the 40s it was Mario who told Dizzy to hire Chano Pozo and so forth and so on and the rest is history. So I met Mario. Mario became my mentor, it was Mario the guy that took me to the union musicians in New York. He recommended me with different musicians in New York, mainly those who went into the recording industry like Arturo Chico O’Farrill to name one of them. But Mario also recommended me to Dizzy Gillespie, something that he never told me. He never mentioned it to me, “I recommended you to Dizzy Gillespie.” He said to me, “I’m going to recommend you to everyone I know here in New York so you’re going to be doing a lot of recordings because you have the ability of sight reading music” and so forth and so on, but he never mentioned Dizzy Gillespie. And one night he just called. We became good friends, and one night Mario called me and I answered the phone and he asked me if I wanted to play with Dizzy Gillespie, which I thought that it was a joke. And he said to me, “No, I’m serious. Dizzy Gillespie needs a drummer for tonight.” Dizzy had an engagement at a club in New York called Fat Tuesday and his regular drummer couldn’t make the gig because he was in Boston and there was a snowstorm and he wasn’t able to make it to New York. So on his desperation, can you

imagine all the drummers that Dizzy had on his phone book. So after calling everybody or I don’t know, whatever, and it turns out that everybody was busy, he remembered, oh Mario told me about a Cuban drummer. So he called Mario and Mario told him, “Let me see if the guy is available.” I was available and that’s how I ended up playing this night, six months after my arrival to the United States I was sitting behind Dizzy Gillespie on drums playing at a club in Manhattan called Fat Tuesday. It was pure luck I think, I will say it is those type of things that when we say you are at the right place at the right time, because I was available, I was at the apartment where I was living. I could have been doing a gig somewhere else and I would have not played with Dizzy that night. I was available and I went to play with Dizzy. So thank you to Mario.
